findings.F1: The result sits on the side the idea predicts but just short of the bar: the pooled 5-day slope is +0.00067 with t 1.90 on 3,419 non-overlapping cases. The quintiles rise from -0.35 % and -0.37 % excess return in the two lowest to +0.27 % and +0.61 % in the two highest, against a per-case standard deviation of about 10 to 12 %, so the data are too noisy to show an effect of this size clearly.
findings.F2: Nearness to the 90-day high carries the effect; the 20-day return adds little. On its own, nearness has a slope t of 2.31 over 5 days (3,419 cases) and 2.58 over 10 days (1,691 cases), while the 20-day return has t 1.40 and 1.07. The two are correlated at 0.62, so adding the weaker term dilutes the stronger one.
findings.F3: The effect is mixed across coins and years rather than absent. Over 5 days the slope is positive on 4 of 6 coins (ETH t 1.52, XRP 1.47, ZEC 1.39, BTC 0.84) and negative on LTC (-0.24) and XMR (-0.72). It is positive in 2019, 2020 (t 2.14), 2021 and 2025, and negative in 2018, 2022 (t -1.99) and 2023 (t -1.98), so each coin and year holds about 570 or 430 cases and too little to decide alone.
findings.F4: The long side carries the slope (t 1.88 on 1,649 positive-forecast cases); the short side shows none (t -0.53 on 1,770 cases). The effect fades by 20 days (t 0.40 on 827 cases), so the move shows over 5 to 10 days.
findings.F5: The idea's size covers the cost of a trade but does not make the book beat holding. Per case the unusual move is +0.43 % (strength 0.034) and the total move +0.47 %, 2.2 and 2.5 times the 0.19 % round trip. Yet the book's Sharpe is 0.42, 0.13 below holding's. The idea is too weak for this sample to confirm, not too small to pay.

ideas.name: near-high momentum, more coins
ideas.idea: The nearer a coin's close sits to its 90-day high and the larger its 20-day return, the higher its return over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should hold a coin longer, and refuse shorts, the closer it is to its 90-day high after a strong 20-day rise.

ideas.idea: The nearer a coin's close sits to its 90-day high, the higher its return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should prefer holding a coin over the coming 10 days the closer its close sits to its 90-day high.
ideas.name: nearness to high, ten days
